title: Auratic Digitalism
oneLiner: Four experiments on whether digital applications can create an aura.

cover.alt: A glowing sphere in turquoise and orange stands on a black stele; a hand hovers above it in the dim light.

facts.Context: Semester project, supervised by Prof. Erich Schöls
facts.Role: Elemental (half), Auragram (development), Tactile (mechanics and Arduino); Artive was built by Juan
facts.Tools: Unity, TouchDesigner, Leap Motion, Arduino, VR, API

sections.label: Aura
text: What fascinates us about an original painting in a museum? Why do we travel for hours to see a building? Walter Benjamin explains the "aura" of such things with their authenticity, uniqueness and distance, and argues that technical reproduction wears it away. Auratic Digitalism asks whether the digital space can nevertheless create an auratic moment, and how.

media.alt: Four black steles in a white room carry the exhibits: a glowing yellow sphere, a phone, a monitor with a black box, and a VR headset.

sections.label: Four exhibits
text: Four exhibits approach this question from different sides. Elemental is a glass sphere that shows natural disasters of fire, water, earth and air, controlled by hand movements over a Leap Motion. Auragram is a smartphone app that works like social media, but turns a photograph into sound instead of showing it. Tactile lets visitors feel music as vibrations in their fingertips. Artive is a VR space in which a painting assembles itself fragment by fragment while a voice tells its background.

media.alt: Elemental: a hand reaches over a sphere glowing in bright turquoise; a Leap Motion lies in front of it.
Auragram: a hand holds a phone whose screen shows a soft yellow-green and violet gradient and the word AURAGRAM.
Tactile: a person reaches with one hand into a black box which is vibrating; a monitor behind it shows pale vertical streaks.
Artive: a person wearing a VR headset holds two controllers.

sections.label: Proof of concept
text: Together the exhibits became a proof of concept: an auratic feeling can be carried into digital media and made tangible, at the intersection of the analogue and digital realm.

media.alt: A person seen from behind reads the black-and-grey project poster with the title Auratic Digitalism.
